publication_verified.title: Output-sensitive sparse factorization over finite fields from dense factorization

values: Uniform deterministic complete factorization, including multiplicities, over every explicitly represented finite field F_(p^m), and construction of irreducibles/extensions of prescribed dense degree without GRH, randomness or an integer-factorization oracle. Additional sparse target: all binary multiplicities with bit cost polynomial in term count, binary exponent length, field encoding and total degree of all distinct densely returned factors.

Output-sensitive sparse factorization over finite fields from dense factorization — Alec Kriebel (ORCID 0009-0001-9320-500X). Preprint/publication date 2026-10-06; production Zenodo publication verified 2026-10-07 UTC. Dense factoring and prescribed-degree construction are inherited OpenAI family142/family029 consequences through Berlekamp, Shoup and Rai. Added sparse numerator/dense denominator descent has degree(V_k)<=kD, at most 2b dense calls of degree <=(b+1)D, b=max(1,ceil(log2(N+1))); arbitrary binary multiplicities and signed artifact cancellation. Construction degree d and optional fixed-root degree r are numeric parameters; no general poly(log d)/poly(log r) or practical-efficiency claim. Two distinct full-package AI adversarial reviews; portability and archival-pointer defects repaired, NEW exact-v5 review passed. Clean reproduction on Python3.11.8/3.14.6; public PDF/archive byte-identical to reviewed files; DOI resolves. Extensive AI use; no conventional human peer review, full Lean verification or first-priority claim. Full Gianni–Trager article inaccessible, bounded primary comparison recorded.
